Refactor internals of libbpf to allow adding custom SEC() handling logic
easily from outside of libbpf. To that effect
registration sets mandatory program type/expected attach type for
a given prefix and can provide three callbacks called at different
points of BPF program lifetime:
- init callback for right after bpf_program is initialized and
prog_type/expected_attach_type is set. This happens during
bpf_object__open() step
column2: close to the very end of constructing

column1: bpf_object
column2: so all the libbpf APIs for querying and updating

column1: bpf_program properties should be available;
- pre-load callback is called right before BPF_PROG_LOAD command is
called in the kernel. This callbacks has ability to set both
bpf_program properties
column2: as well as program load attributes

column1: and augmenting the standard libbpf handling of them;
- optional auto-attach callback
column2: which makes a given SEC() handler

column1: support auto-attachment of a BPF program through bpf_program__attach()
API and/or BPF skeletons <skel>__attach() method.
Each callbacks gets a `long cookie` parameter passed in
specified during SEC() handling. This can be used by callbacks to lookup
whatever additional information is necessary.
This is not yet completely ready to be exposed to the outside world
mainly due to non-public nature of struct bpf_prog_load_params. Instead
of making it part of public API
column2: we'll wait until the planned low-level

column1: libbpf API improvements for BPF_PROG_LOAD and other typical bpf()
syscall APIs
column2: at which point we'll have a public

column1: way to fully specify BPF program load parameters
an interface for custom pre-load callbacks.
But this change itself is already a good first step to unify the BPF
program hanling logic even within the libbpf itself. As one example
the extra per-program type handling (sleepable bit
resolution
column2: unsetting optional expected attach type) is now more obvious

column1: and is gathered in one place.
